newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Lagoven ups output potential, sales.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Lagoven ups output potential, sales.

text.p: State-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) subsidiary Lagoven said it increased potential production in 1996 by 98,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 1.330 million (bpd).
Operating contracts with private foreign companies at upgraded fields also boosted output by an average 62,000 bpd, ten times more than in 1995, Lagoven president Julius Trinkunas said.

A statement released Wednesday quoting Trinkunas' end-of-year message to staff said Lagoven's proven reserves increased 695 million barrels to 27.351 billion barrels. Gas reserves totalled 38.5 billion cubic feet.
Trinkunas forecast potential oil production "to reach about 2.100 million (bpd) in the mid-term."
Exports this year were 1.049 million bpd, of which 706,000 bpd was crude. He gave no comparative figures.
Lagoven, the largest of PDVSA's operating companies, also said it significantly raised total sales this year to $7.28 billion, up from $5.46 billion in 1995.
Net profits rose to $1.32 billion, up $784 million on last year. "This allowed Lagoven, for the fourth consecutive year, to achieve financial self-sufficiency," Trinkunas said.

He said Lagoven's rate of return on net capital employed, measured in dollars, was 14.8 percent for 1996, stressing this compared favorably with the world's leading oil companies whose indicator was about 12 percent.

The company's Amuay refinery, in the western state of Falcon, processed an average 485,000 bpd, up 10,000 bpd compared with 1995. Of that total, Trinkunas said 125,000 bpd was heavy crude, a 25 percent rise over last year.
